A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Thera by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison despite substantial reformatting and figure renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B–C report original super-resolution results, PSNR/SSIM measurements, multi-scale consistency experiments and component ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports interpolation-baseline results and computational measurements in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The thermal activations, shared frequency bank, hypernetwork, TV prior and S/M/L architectures remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix D. Changed channel labels in v2 Figure 8 conflict with the retained architecture description and do not establish an actual model revision.

E1.justification: Both train on DIV2K and evaluate DIV2K, Set5, Set14, BSDS100, Urban100 and Manga109, including out-of-distribution scaling factors. Additional illustrations and computational measurements introduce no distinct dataset, domain or task.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains bicubic, MetaSR, LIIF, LTE, CUF, CiaoSR and CLIT. V2 adds a conventional baseline combining each fixed ×4 backbone with Lanczos resampling.

E3.justification: V2 introduces the fixed-×4-backbone resampling comparison and training-time, inference-time and memory evaluation using EDSR-baseline on RTX 3090 Ti GPUs. Existing data splits, training budgets, preprocessing, PSNR/SSIM evaluation and self-ensembling settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds computational-efficiency analysis in Appendix F, expands Figure 3's anti-aliasing comparisons and adds a non-integer-scale showcase. It removes v1 Section 3.1's report of unsuccessful heat-equation-residual regularization. The principal ablations and multi-scale consistency experiments remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2 introduces no statistical uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: All previously reported scores in Tables 1–6 are retained. V2 adds interpolation scores, computational measurements in Table 7 and qualitative outputs. At ×30, the new interpolation baseline exceeds Thera-L with EDSR-baseline (20.62 versus 20.61 dB) and SwinIR (20.82 versus 20.79 dB).

T1.justification: The heat-equation construction, Gaussian-kernel derivation, diffusivity formulas, sampling relationship and frequency-initialization rule are retained. V2 clarifies notation and rectangular image domains without changing the existing equal-sampling assumption or introducing new proofs.

C1.justification: V2 explicitly claims in the Introduction that Thera is the first neural-field method allowing bandwidth control at test time. The central claims about Gaussian anti-aliasing, arbitrary-scale super-resolution and parameter efficiency remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 attributes weaker ×2 performance more specifically to anisotropy from the oriented pixel grid. It interprets the new interpolation comparison as evidence of learned scale-specific priors and explicitly explains that modulating deeper fields would lose the anti-aliasing guarantee.

D1.justification: V1 promises a future public code/checkpoint release; v2 supplies a repository address and states availability. Appendix F adds hardware and computational requirements. Section 4.1 corrects Thera-S's parameter total from 8,192 to 8,256, consistent with the architecture already documented in v1.

R1.justification: V2 adds BACON, Polynomial Neural Fields, Modulated Periodic Activations and Neural Fourier Filter Bank. The added discussion distinguishes continuous test-time bandwidth control from fixed subband decompositions and deeper modulated representations, providing a limited expansion of research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 extensively revises paragraphs throughout the abstract, introduction, method, results and limitations, clarifying parameter roles and refining the explanatory narrative. The principal section sequence remains intact, but the editorial rewriting extends well beyond isolated corrections.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a single-column layout, redraws Figures 1, 2 and 4, expands Figures 3 and 7, and adds Figure 6 and Table 7. Qualitative panels are reformatted and expanded. Renumbered Figure 8 introduces incorrect repeated 64-channel labels where v1 Figure 6 showed 96/128-channel stages.

improvement.justification: The added interpolation control, computational reporting, clearer exposition and stated code/checkpoint access provide a limited improvement in evaluability and reproducibility around an unchanged method. These gains are tempered by superiority statements that are not fully reconciled with the new ×30 baseline wins and incorrect channel labels in Figure 8.
